## **5.3 Business Rules Testing** {#5.3-business-rules-testing}

Business rules testing validates the domain-specific constraints that govern how ForeSeeMe handles healthcare data. These rules are distinct from general functional behaviour — they define the system's correctness boundaries. For example, it is a business rule that an adherence log's document ID must be a deterministic composite of medicationId, date, and reminderTime; it is a business rule that an unauthenticated request must never reach a user's Firestore sub-collection; and it is a business rule that a medication with isActive \= false must never generate a dose card in the daily check-in schedule.

The five business rule test blocks below focus on authentication rules, medication data integrity, adherence logging constraints, notification lifecycle rules, and user data isolation requirements.

**Business Rules Testing 1: Authentication Rules**

**Related Requirement:** BR-1 – Authentication Business Rules

**Testing Objective:** To verify that the system enforces all authentication and session management rules.

| No. | Test Case / Test Script | Attribute and value | Expected Result | Actual Result |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | :---: |
| 1 | Attempt login with unverified / unregistered e-mail | Unknown email address | Login rejected; error message displayed | **Pass** |
| 2 | Attempt to access protected screen without session | No auth token | Redirected to login; access denied | **Pass** |
| 3 | Logout clears all session data | Logout tapped | UID cleared; stream closed; login shown | **Pass** |
| 4 | Session cookie persists across background / foreground | App suspended then resumed | Session intact; no re-login required | **Pass** |

**Business Rules Testing 2: Medication Data Integrity Rules**

**Related Requirement:** BR-2 – Medication Data Rules

**Testing Objective:** To confirm the system enforces all business constraints around medication data creation and modification.

| No. | Test Case / Test Script | Attribute and value | Expected Result | Actual Result |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | :---: |
| 1 | Medication name must not be empty | name \= "" | Save rejected; name error shown | **Pass** |
| 2 | At least one reminder time is required | reminderTimes \= \[\] | Save rejected; reminder error shown | **Pass** |
| 3 | Reminder time stored in HH:mm 24-hour format | User selects 08:00 AM | Stored as "08:00" in Firestore | **Pass** |
| 4 | Medication isActive defaults to true on creation | New document created | isActive field \= true in Firestore | **Pass** |
| 5 | Medication document includes createdAt timestamp | Document saved | createdAt present and correctly formatted | **Pass** |

**Business Rules Testing 3: Adherence Logging Rules**

**Related Requirement:** BR-3 – Adherence Business Rules

**Testing Objective:** To verify that adherence logs follow the deterministic ID scheme and prevent duplicate entries.

| No. | Test Case / Test Script | Attribute and value | Expected Result | Actual Result |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | :---: |
| 1 | Adherence log ID \= medicationId \+ date \+ reminderTime | Known medication, date, time | Document ID matches composite key exactly | **Pass** |
| 2 | Duplicate check-in overwrites existing log, not creates new | Same composite key submitted twice | Single document in Firestore; updated status | **Pass** |
| 3 | Pending status set by default before user action | Dose card opened | Default status \= Pending visible on card | **Pass** |
| 4 | Taken and Skipped are the only permitted final states | Attempt to set invalid status | Invalid status rejected by repository | **Pass** |

**Business Rules Testing 4: Notification Scheduling Rules**

**Related Requirement:** BR-4 – Notification Business Rules

**Testing Objective:** To confirm notifications are scheduled and cancelled in accordance with medication lifecycle rules.

| No. | Test Case / Test Script | Attribute and Value | Expected Result | Actual Result |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | :---: |
| 1 | Notification scheduled immediately on medication save | Medication saved successfully | Notification present in scheduler post-save | **Pass** |
| 2 | Notification repeats daily at same time | Next day checked | Notification fires again at scheduled time | **Pass** |
| 3 | Notification cancelled when medication deleted | Delete confirmed | Notification absent from scheduler | **Pass** |
| 4 | Notification cancelled when medication deactivated | isActive \= false | Notification absent from scheduler | **Pass** |
| 5 | New notification scheduled when reminder time edited | Reminder time changed | New notification at updated time present | **Pass** |

**Business Rules Testing 5: Data Privacy and User Isolation Rules**

**Related Requirement:** BR-5 – Data Privacy Rules

**Testing Objective:** To ensure user data isolation is enforced at the Firestore rules layer.

| No. | Test Case / Test Script | Attribute and value | Expected Result | Actual Result |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | :---: |
| 1 | Users can only read medications under own UID | Query with own UID | Data returned successfully | **Pass** |
| 2 | Users cannot read medications under another UID | Query with foreign UID | Firestore rules deny read | **Pass** |
| 3 | Users can only write adherence logs under own UID | Write with own UID | Write permitted | **Pass** |
| 4 | Unauthenticated request blocked by Firestore rules | No auth header | Read / write denied | **Pass** |

## **5.4 Integration Testing** {#5.4-integration-testing}

Integration testing examines how ForeSeeMe's modules interact with one another as a system. Individual units may pass in isolation and still fail when combined — and in a reactive, stream-driven architecture like ForeSeeMe's, integration points between the Firebase Auth layer, Riverpod providers, GoRouter, Firestore repositories, and the notification service are particularly important to exercise explicitly.

The seven integration test blocks below trace vertical slices through the system: from authentication to Firestore data loading, from medication save to dose card generation, from save to notification scheduling, from check-in action to adherence log creation, from Riverpod state change to UI rebuild, from Firebase auth state to GoRouter redirect, and finally a complete end-to-end healthcare workflow executed on the physical OPPO Reno12 5G device.

**Integration Testing 1: Authentication → Firestore Data Load**

**Related Requirement:** FR-1.1, FR-2.7 – Auth and Stream Integration

**Testing Objective:** To verify that successful authentication immediately triggers the correct Firestore data stream for the authenticated user.

| No. | Test Case / Test Script | Attribute and value | Expected Result | Actual Result |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | :---: |
| 1 | Login with valid credentials; observe medication stream | Correct UID propagated to provider | Medication stream starts; UI populated | **Pass** |
| 2 | Login with Google; observe medication stream | Google UID propagated | Same stream behaviour as email login | **Pass** |
| 3 | Logout; observe stream state | Auth state cleared | Stream closes; UI shows empty / login screen | **Pass** |
| 4 | Login as different user; check data isolation | User B logs in after User A | User B sees only their own medications | **Pass** |

**Integration Testing 2: Medication Save → Check-In Generation**

**Related Requirement:** FR-2.1, FR-3.1 – Save and Schedule Integration

**Testing Objective:** To confirm that saving a new medication automatically produces dose cards in the daily Check-In screen.

| No. | Test Case / Test Script | Attribute and Value | Expected Result | Actual Result |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | :---: |
| 1 | Save once-daily medication; open Check-In | One reminder time | One dose card shown for today | **Pass** |
| 2 | Save twice-daily medication; open Check-In | Two reminder times | Two dose cards shown for today | **Pass** |
| 3 | Save medication for tomorrow; open Check-In for today | Start date is tomorrow | No card shown for today | **Pass** |
| 4 | Delete medication; verify Check-In updates | Medication removed from Firestore | Dose card removed from Check-In | **Pass** |

**Integration Testing 3: Medication Save → Notification Scheduling**

**Related Requirement:** FR-2.1, FR-4.1 – Save and Notification Integration

**Testing Objective:** To verify that saving a medication automatically schedules a local notification for each reminder time.

| No. | Test Case / Test Script | Attribute and value | Expected Result | Actual Result |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | :---: |
| 1 | Save medication; verify notification in scheduler | Save completes successfully | Notification ID present in pending list | **Pass** |
| 2 | Update reminder time; verify old notification cancelled | Reminder time changed | Old notification gone; new one scheduled | **Pass** |
| 3 | Delete medication; verify notification cancelled | Medication document deleted | Notification ID absent from pending list | **Pass** |
| 4 | Deactivate medication; verify notification cancelled | isActive \= false | Notification cancelled without delete | **Pass** |

**Integration Testing 4: Check-In Action → Adherence Log → Riverpod State**

**Related Requirement:** FR-3.2, FR-3.3 – Adherence Integration

**Testing Objective:** To confirm that check-in actions propagate correctly from UI through Riverpod to Firestore and back.

| No. | Test Case / Test Script | Attribute and value | Expected Result | Actual Result |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | :---: |
| 1 | Tap Taken; verify Firestore log created | AdherenceNotifier called | Log document with status=Taken written | **Pass** |
| 2 | Tap Skipped; verify Firestore log created | AdherenceNotifier called | Log document with status=Skipped written | **Pass** |
| 3 | Mark same dose twice; verify no duplicate | Duplicate attempt | Existing log updated; no second document | **Pass** |
| 4 | Verify deterministic ID format in log document | medicationId+date+reminderTime | Document ID matches expected composite key | **Pass** |

**Integration Testing 5: Riverpod State → UI Reactive Rebuild**

**Related Requirement:** FR-2.7, FR-3.3 – Reactive Architecture Integration

**Testing Objective:** To ensure that Riverpod provider state changes trigger correct UI rebuilds without manual refresh.

| No. | Test Case / Test Script | Attribute and value | Expected Result | Actual Result |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | :---: |
| 1 | Add medication via repository; observe medication screen | Provider state updated | New card appears without page reload | **Pass** |
| 2 | Toggle theme; observe app-wide re-render | ThemeProvider notified | All screens switch theme simultaneously | **Pass** |
| 3 | Record adherence log; observe card status update | AdherenceProvider notified | Dose card badge updates immediately | **Pass** |
| 4 | Switch date on Check-In; observe dose card refresh | Date changed in state | Correct doses for new date displayed | **Pass** |

**Integration Testing 6: Firebase Auth State → GoRouter Guard**

**Related Requirement:** FR-1.4, FR-6.1 – Auth State and Routing Integration

**Testing Objective:** To verify that GoRouter redirect logic responds correctly to all Firebase authentication state transitions.

| No. | Test Case / Test Script | Attribute and value | Expected Result | Actual Result |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | :---: |
| 1 | App starts with no session; observe initial route | No Firebase user | Router directs to /login | **Pass** |
| 2 | Login completes; observe route change | Auth state changes to authenticated | Router navigates to /home automatically | **Pass** |
| 3 | Logout triggered; observe route change | Auth state cleared | Router navigates to /login automatically | **Pass** |
| 4 | Deep link to /checkin while unauthenticated | No session active | Redirected to /login; intent preserved | **Pass** |

**Integration Testing 7: Full End-to-End Healthcare Workflow**

**Related Requirement:** FR-1.1, FR-2.1, FR-3.1, FR-3.2, FR-4.1 – Complete Workflow

**Testing Objective:** To validate the complete ForeSeeMe user journey from registration through to adherence logging and notification receipt.

| No. | Test Case / Test Script | Attribute and Value | Expected Result | Actual Result |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | :---: |
| 1 | Register → Login → Add medication → Open Check-In | All steps performed in sequence | Each step succeeds; dose card shown | **Pass** |
| 2 | Check-In → Mark Taken → Verify Firestore log | Taken tapped on dose card | Adherence log document created correctly | **Pass** |
| 3 | Notification fires → User taps it → App opens | Reminder delivered at scheduled time | App opens to Check-In screen | **Pass** |
| 4 | Complete workflow on real device (OPPO Reno5 5G) | Physical device test | All steps pass without crash or data error | **Pass** |
| 5 | Switch theme mid-session; verify no data loss | Theme toggled during active session | Theme changes; all medication data intact | **Pass** |

## **5.5 Testing Summary and Evaluation** {#5.5-testing-summary-and-evaluation}

The testing process described in this chapter covered all functional modules implemented during the 30% milestone of the ForeSeeMe project. The results are summarised below.

| Testing Category | Total Test Cases | Cases Passed | Cases Failed | Pass Rate |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | :---: |
| Unit Testing | 64 | 64 | 0 | **Pass** |
| Functional Testing | 46 | 46 | 0 | **Pass** |
| Business Rules Testing | 22 | 22 | 0 | **Pass** |
| Integration Testing | 30 | 30 | 0 | **Pass** |
| Total | 162 | 162 | 0 | **Pass** |

All 162 test cases passed with no failures recorded during the testing phase. The results confirm that the ForeSeeMe authentication system, medication management module, daily check-in workflow, local notification service, theme management system, and navigation guard are all operating correctly at the current implementation milestone.

Several defects that were discovered and resolved during development are worth noting. Silent Firestore save failures were caused by exception swallowing inside the Riverpod notifier and were fixed by introducing explicit error propagation through the repository chain. Medication dose cards were initially disappearing from the Check-In screen due to an overly strict createdAt timestamp filter; this was corrected by simplifying the active medication scheduling predicate. Android notification delays were addressed by enabling exactAllowWhileIdle scheduling and requesting the exact alarm permission at runtime on Android 13\. Google Sign-In failures were resolved by correcting the SHA-1 key registered with the Firebase project. These fixes were all verified through the test cases documented in this chapter.

The testing coverage achieved at this milestone provides a strong foundation for the 60–100% implementation phases, where additional modules — including the AI disease prediction engine, analytics dashboard, adherence scoring system, and Firebase Cloud Messaging — will require their own dedicated testing chapters. The architecture's modular, feature-first structure means each new module can be tested independently before integration, maintaining the same level of confidence demonstrated here.

## **5.6 Testing Environment** {#5.6-testing-environment}

All testing was conducted in the following environment:

| Parameter | Detail |
| ----- | ----- |
| Primary Test Device | OPPO Reno5 5G |
| Operating System | Android 13 |
| Flutter SDK Version | Flutter 3.x (stable channel) |
| Firebase Project Region | asia-south1 (Mumbai) |
| Backend Database | Cloud Firestore (NoSQL) |
| State Management | Riverpod (reactive architecture) |
| Navigation | GoRouter |
| Notifications Package | flutter\_local\_notifications \+ timezone |
| Test Execution Method | Manual on-device testing |
| IDE | Visual Studio Code with Flutter/Dart extensions |
